title: NASA Crashed a Spacecraft Into an Asteroid at 14,000 mph. On Purpose

scenes.text: NASA crashed a spacecraft into an asteroid at 14,000 miles an hour.
On purpose. To see if we could shove one off course.
The spacecraft weighed about 500 kilograms. The asteroid was 525 feet across.
Almost seven million miles away, it hit dead on, and blew a tail of rock 19,000 miles long into space.
The asteroid's orbit shortened by 32 minutes. The first time humans ever moved a space rock.
So if one ever comes for us, we've practiced. At 14,000 miles an hour.

description:
In September 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft hit the asteroid Dimorphos at about 14,000 miles an hour, on purpose.
The roughly 500 kilogram spacecraft struck the 525-foot asteroid almost seven million miles from Earth. The impact threw out a debris tail at least 19,000 miles long and shortened the asteroid's orbit around its partner by 32 minutes, the first time humans have measurably changed the motion of a space object.
If an asteroid were headed for Earth, would you trust this to work? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: NASA HIT AN ASTEROID AT 14,000 MPH
first_comment: The spacecraft sent back pictures right up to the last second, until the asteroid filled the whole frame. Would you want years of warning for an incoming asteroid, or none at all?
